overview: A strong acid ionizes essentially completely in water, while a weak acid ionizes only partially, establishing a dynamic equilibrium.
genZNote: Strong acids give it all up in water. Weak acids only ionize part-time.

aspects.label: Degree of Ionization
aspects.valueB: Only partially ionized (small degree of dissociation, α < 1).

aspects.label: Equilibrium Constant
aspects.valueA: Ka is very large (essentially undefined/not meaningfully tabulated since reaction goes to completion).
aspects.valueB: Ka has a small, measurable finite value.
